Subject: NeuroNova eval onboarding — model recommendations & dataset checklist

Hi Dana / Matt,

Thanks again for taking time earlier — great conversation and clear signals that NeuroNova has a concrete production use case for clinical triage summarization. Below is a short post-call recap, recommended next steps for the model-fit evaluation on Redwood, and a checklist for the sample dataset we need to kick off an automated benchmark run.

Recap (1-line): you want a low-latency assistant that extracts structured triage fields and produces a concise narrative summary from triage notes, with an initial focus on cardiology flows.

Recommended models to evaluate (prioritized):
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (best balance of accuracy on short instruction tasks)
- Llama-3-8B (8-bit quantized) for faster throughput and lower cost during the bulk run
- Llama-2-13B (low-precision quantized variant) for fallback when longer-context completeness is required

Why these: they provide different trade-offs across latency/cost/accuracy — we usually run the smaller instruct model first to establish scoring baselines, then test the 13B variant on failure cases.

Quick benchmarking links: Redwood public perf profiles (redwood dashboard) — https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/mistral-7b; evaluation runner for this deal — https://redwood.example.com/eval-runner/NNH-2193

Dataset checklist (what we need from NeuroNova to run a canonical eval):
- 1–2k representative records (CSV) with columns: input_text, gold_summary, triage_code, patient_age_group, specialty_tag
- Gold labels: target_summary and structured triage fields (CSV or JSONL) for scoring
- Note: do not include full PHI — if necessary, mark fields with flagged_pii=YES and include a redacted version; we can handle masked PHI in the Private/Dedicated deployment.

Scoring & quality checks we suggest:
- ROUGE-L and BERTScore for summary fidelity
- Field-level exact-match + relaxed-match (fuzzy) for triage_code and structured outputs
- Human spot-check on a 150-record stratified sample (we recommend labeling 3 raters per record)

Attachments: sample dataset template (neuronova_sample_dataset.csv), prompt bank v1 (prompt_bank_v1.md), scoring matrix (eval_scoring_matrix.xlsx) — see attached stubs and the Drive folder link.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) NeuroNova: share 1–2k de-identified sample by EOD Thu (S3 link or Drive).
2) Redwood: perform a 48–72 hour automated run across the 3 candidate models, surface per-model metrics + failure cases, and propose a production configuration (batching, quantization profile).
3) Alignment call: 30 minutes to review scoring results & select pilot model (we suggest Fri or next Tue).

Please confirm dataset timeline and whether we should route the eval through a Private deployment (if you prefer samples never leave your VPC). Happy to loop in our SE (Rishi) for technical onboarding — cc'd.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor

Hi Dana / Matt — looping in Rishi (SE) and Marissa (CS) to address the technical and labeling/process questions. Short answers below, plus concrete onboarding steps.

1) Private VPC eval: yes — Redwood Private supports short-run evals inside a customer VPC. For a 2k-record automated run we can deploy a temporary Private worker set (no model weights leave your network) and deliver metrics + failure-case artifacts. We typically do this under a short SOW or a pilot contract; Neha can share a templated MSA addendum.

2) Latency: p95 < 250ms at 200 tokens is achievable on Dedicated for the smaller models (Mistral-7B / Llama-3-8B quantized) with tuned batching (batch size 4–8) and our low-latency kernel path. The 13B variant will be higher; expect p95 ~350–450ms depending on instance type. We can test a few config knobs in the run and publish per-model SLOs.

3) Human spot-check / disagreement handling: our recommended approach:
- Have 3 independent raters per sample
- Use majority vote as primary resolution; capture Cohen's Kappa per label to quantify agreement
- For tied cases, route to a senior annotator (tier-2) — we can provide tooling (simple web UI) and an audit CSV of adjudicated records. Marissa can run the spot-check program and provide the tie-breaker workflow.

Onboarding steps (technical):
- Provide 2k de-identified sample (CSV) in the template schema to the Drive folder or grant S3 access to redwood-eval@redwood-samples (we'll share a presigned S3 if preferred).
- Confirm whether you want the run in Private VPC or Redwood-hosted test. If Private, we'll need a short network setup call (30m).
- We run the baseline suite (Mistral-7B-Instruct, Llama-3-8B-q8, Llama-2-13B-q4) and return a results package: per-record outputs, metric aggregation, top-50 failure cases, and recommended production config.

I've attached the scoring rubric and a prompt bank — these are starter artifacts; feel free to edit. If you'd like, Rishi can schedule a 30-minute tech onboarding tomorrow morning PST.

Next step for Redwood: schedule the network/setup call if Private is required. Neha — can you confirm procurement cadence so we have a timing estimate for the pilot SOW?

Thanks,
